videos.title: So what’s the real difference between grass fed and grain fed red meat?
videos.description:
I just read a research review that summarized the differences between the two.

Unsurprisingly, they found that grass fed meat has less total fat.

The grass fed meat also had higher Omega-3s, which are anti-inflammatory.

On the other hand, the grain fed meat had more Omega 6s, which are inflammatory.

So the grass fed meat has less total fat AND a better healthy fat profile.

This can help protect against cancer and heart disease.

Yes, grass fed meat is more expensive, but you can choose cuts that are less expensive (tri-tip, skirt steak, ground beef), and cook them slowly to tenderize (for example, putting a tri-tip in a sous vide machine makes the tough cut more tender).

So, enjoy that grass fed red meat, shop locally when you can, and get healthier.

videos.title: “Everything in moderation” is a lie.
videos.description:
It’s just not possible. At least for most of us.

For a lot of folks going through a weight loss journey, it’s not just weight loss—it’s an addiction recovery process.

So, if we have this expectation on ourselves that we should just be able to eat “everything in moderation,” it really sets us up for frustration and failure.

It’s just not possible.

We’re surrounded by foods created by Big Food and Big Pharma that are so appealing and convenient.

They’re hyperpalatable and triggering, and they’re actually designed and created so that we can’t physically eat them in moderation.

It’s just not possible.

It’s like telling an alcoholic that they should be able to consume just one glass of wine a night or something’s wrong with them.

Nothing is wrong with them. Their body is just wired to over consume alcohol.

The same thing happens with food. A lot of us are wired to over consume these foods—especially when they’re hyperpalatable.

If you’ve been trying so hard to eat everything in moderation and you just haven’t succeeded, I want you to know it’s not your fault.

The ticket to success? SAY NO.

Moderation isn’t possible. Say NO to those foods that don’t love you back.

That is a form of self-respect.

videos.title: 3 Breakfast Foods You Should Avoid on Your Weight Loss Journey
videos.description:
“Dr. Ashley, after I eat breakfast, I feel bloated and tired. What should I be eating?”

Breakfast is not the most important meal of the day, but it is the most important meal to get RIGHT.

We sometimes fill this meal with sugary, starchy foods instead of whole, nutrient-dense ones, causing us to feel bloated and tired.

It is important to start your day with foods that will nourish your body.

Stay away from breakfast foods like:
Corn flakes with milk
Fruit flavored yogurt
Fruit smoothies
Oatmeal with fruit

These foods will mess with your blood sugar, causing it to be high then low.

This causes your body to NOT burn fat for fuel.

The good news is that finding foods to eat that will keep your energy up throughout the day and allow you to burn fat is easier than you think.

Here are 3 breakfast foods I recommend to all of my clients:

→Eggs, eggs, and MORE EGGS!

You can scramble them, poach them, or make tasty omelets.

→Full fat plain Greek yogurt

Add berries, nuts, or seeds if you like!

→A smoothie….but protein based, not carb loaded.

Get rid of the fruit juice and frozen mango! Use unsweetened almond or coconut milk, frozen berries, spinach, and a protein source, like a protein powder.

videos.title: Why are you not losing weight! 🏃🏻‍♀️
videos.description:
Why are you not losing weight! 🏃🏻‍♀️

If the scale is not moving, it is usually not because you are lazy or doing nothing. It is because your body is getting mixed signals.

When your days feel unpredictable, your hunger feels louder, your cravings feel stronger, and your belly feels like the last place to change. Then you try to fix it by cutting harder, and the cycle gets worse.

The people who lose weight for real are not “more disciplined.” They remove the daily friction that keeps the body in stop-start mode. They make their week boring on purpose, so the results become predictable.

If you feel like you are trying harder than everyone else and getting less progress, it is time to figure out what is driving your pattern.

videos.title: New Study on Mice and Why we need to Eat Adequate Protein
videos.description:
No, we are not mice, but we can learn a lot from them!

I was just reviewing a 2023 mouse study and gleaned a lot of helpful information.

This study looked at the amount of protein required to support the metabolic health of these mice as they were aging.

They fed all the mice the same amount of calories but varied the percentage of protein:

5%
15%
25%
35%
45%

They found that, as the protein intake decreased, the mice were hungrier and progressively ate more.

The mice on the lower protein percentage diets also had fatty liver.

Conversely, the mice on the higher protein diets had better blood glucose and better blood lipid control.

And the creatinine levels in the mice on the 45% protein diet were the lowest which shows that high protein intake does not cause renal impairment.

(If you’ve heard that higher protein intake causes kidney issues, that’s a MYTH.)

The moral of the story: the mice had better metabolic health when they consumed more protein.

This seems to be the case for us humans as well. So we want to make sure we’re consuming about 0.8 to 1.0 gram of protein per pound OPTIMAL body weight every day.
